reviews.The Hero of Ages:
I did not enjoy this book. Not because it's "bad", because let's face it, Sanderson at his worst is ten times better than most fantasy authors. However, in my opinion this series is too long for what it has to say. You could easily erase the events of the previous book and extract the little things that actually matter from it to tell them on this third book which could also be trimmed by much. 
Besides the length, there are some other issues that bothered me a lot. First, vin's character and role was carefully developed through the series as a skilled warrior with unprecedented power. You believe she is so because you saw her grow and it's one of the things that i really liked about this series but in this book elend is a Mistborn too and he steals much of her thunder. Even Though it is remarked that vin is considerably more skilled than him, he is more powerful than her. This was annoying for me because Elend's personality does not fit the role and i quite liked that he was the scholar and Vin was the warrior. Not everyone has to have superpowers (although i expected Elend to be a Misting of one of the weird metals) but him being this new warrior and fighting all the time ruined things for me. 
Spook was the real surprise for me this time around. I always liked his character and wanted more from him but here he truly becomes his own man. He introduces us to this new concept of Mistings who burn their metals for too long which i thought was utterly cool and overall I really enjoyed his development during this book and his role in the ending which to me was very satisfying.
The bad guys i did not enjoy at all. First there's Quellion (the citizen) whose reason for being an asshole i will not reveal because of spoilers but let's just say it ruined him for me completely. Then there's Yomen, the lord ruler's final fangirl. He debates quite often with elend about the lord ruler and for some reason they never say anything about the oppression upon the ska.   
The only two things that i did like about this book was Spook  and the ending which i found was unexpected and refreshing.
All in all this entry didn't change my opinion about the series; Amazing magic system, cool world building, too long, not believable and sadly overrated.
reviews.Edgedancer:
I really enjoyed this book. 
I felt like the lift's interlude in words of radiance was one of the best chapters in the series so far and i was really happy when i discovered that this novella existed. 
Overall the story is really fun and quick paced, and it adds some new layers to the epic array of characters this story has. 
There are some interesting events that occur through the end of the book that further develop the big story of the stormlight archive, especially regarding a certain character's change of mind which i am told could be very confusing in oathbringer to those who skipped edgedancer. Therefore, read it!
reviews.Mistborn: The Final Empire:
i've read most of Sanderson's main series: Elantris, Warbreaker, steelheart and of course Stormlight Archive and they are all amazing! The stronger elements they all have in common being the cohesive and believable world building,  the originality and deepness of the magic systems and the relatable characters. I'm happy to say that in all these categories Mistborn certainly does not disappoint.
There are some motives that seem to come back in his books (an oppressed race, a slave fueled by dreams of revenge, a godlike ruler) which kind of bothered me at first but enough new concepts are introduced for me to almost forget this.   
All characters are awesome and likeable. There's this gang of superpowered dudes that are kind of like a family and by the end of the book you really feel close to each and everyone of them.
The pace of the book felt rather slow but as is the Sanderson way, when you reach the last fourth of the book shit starts hitting the fan and the pace goes nuts, throwing you all kinds of crazy events and twists.
In short, this is a very original fantasy story with a really cool magic system, awesome characters and cool twists.
reviews.The Wise Man's Fear:
Let me start by saying that i hated this book. Plain and simple.
I wanted to like it though. i really did. 
i figured that the first book was only an introduction to something bigger and that all the subjects that were touched and left unresolved would further develop in the second book. The thing is that the second book feels like a second introduction or even worse like it was pointless. 
The hero has a very clear purpose which is to find the chandrion who are this gang of mythical characters who murdered his family. That being said in the 994 pages of this book (or the 43 hrs or so of the audiobook) this subject is barely touched. It is always reminded that this is the main plot theme but nothing happens regarding this. 
It is basically a recollection of pointless adventures of a 16 years old kid(or god if you consider that he can do almost anything amazingly) who is painfully caught in the friend zone of an obnoxious girl.
Seriously... most of the book is about this "will they - won't they" relationship with this dena girl and it is so repetitive that it makes me wanna bash my head on the closest wall.
I wouldn't mind so much about the absence of a main plot development if these side gigs were somewhat pointing to some meaning or some reason for me hearing this story in the first place but instead they each become increasingly random and pointless.
What's even worse is the portrayal of women in this book. At first it didn't bother me much but then i realized that all the women in this book are described in a very shallow and sexist way. Even those that are powerful are pictured as seductresses, manipulative or simply objectified by men.
In the end i finished the book having more questions than when i finished the last one, i felt like it went absolutely nowhere and that so many cool ideas were left undeveloped or misused. The only reason i am not giving this book 1 star is because it is well written. It is in my opinion pointless well written randomness.  :)
reviews.Prince of Thorns:
This is a very unique book. 

I stumbled upon this while looking for a good fantasy book with an evil protagonist. This is something i always wanted to read and prince of thorns is just that.

jorg, the main character is an asshole. No doubt about it. However, eventhough you can never truly justify his behaviour, you learn the very reasons for him becoming the way he is and you get to understand him.

If you fear that you might not be satisfied with just one evil character, well you are in luck because almost every other character in this books is an asshole. Jorg's gang, Jorg's father, the necromancers....plenty of evil to go arround.

The setting itself felt a little dull at first. It felt like just another pseudo medieval time period with some slight magical elements but the more i advanced in the story i realized it was much more than that. There is a twist in the middle of the book that changes things and it's pretty cool. i won't say more beyond that. 

The writing style is quiet good in my opinion and the audiobook's narrator is great. I also found that in comparison to other fantasy writers who tend to overly describe small events and encounters in order to further develop the setting, Mark Lawrence's work feels focused and although there are some side events, they seem meaningfull.

I loved this book. I can't wait to read the sequels. I can strongly recommend this to anyone wanting to step in the shoes of the bad guy for a change. Beware though that this are some unsettling and violent little shoes to step in.
reviews.Assassin's Apprentice:
To be honest i am not sure how much i actually enjoyed this book but I decided to give it 5 stars because i truly think it is quite brilliant. 
The story is told in the first person perspective which tends to be tricky in the fantasy genre and yet here it is done flawlessly. The narrator engages the reader in a way that makes you feel like you are sitting by the bonfire listening to an old taleteller's voice (especially if you are listening to the audiobook which is what i did). Basically you always follow the main character's journey like a memoir of sorts. However, at times (many times in fact) i found myself struggling to enjoy the story due to the main character. He just didn't quite resonate with me.
The hero in the story is kind of like a young tarzan or mowgli. Not because he is wild but because he lived a simple life and is suddenly thrown into the royal world with it's complicated sets of rules and etiquette. He is naive and pure. So much so that it becomes infuriating. There are times when a normal person would get angry and yet he just accepts things or gets mildly frustrated and this made it really hard for me to enjoy his tale.
This is not to say that the character is not developed properly. In fact, i think that the author did a wonderful job of imagining a character like this and you really be
reviews.Bird Box:
For some reason this book is on almost every list for the top horror books and it really baffles me. It might be a good book but to put it right next to any Stephen King book for example, is insane. The only remarkable thing about this book is the idea behind it which is truly something i haven't seen before; a world in which seeing causes madness. Sounds cool, right?
Well the execution however, is lacking in almost every way. 
The whole "Horror" theme here rides on the idea that there might be something next to you that you can't see and seeing it would be the end of you. The scenes usually go like this: someone hears something weird, they start to overthink, they freak out and in the end it's usually either a false alarm or nothing that bad. Which is understandable from their perspective, as i'm sure anyone would become paranoid in that situation but it gets old real quick. There is tension but there's not much release.
Then there is a certain plot twist(which i am not going to reveal) that pisses me off so much. The author gives you a certain clue that for me, it spoiled the hell out of that twist. If it had been a little more subtle then maybe but i just knew right a way what the twist was gonna be. 
I don't know. The books is written pretty well and the concept is original but the story itself is  nothing special in my opinion.
reviews.The Blade Itself:
it's been a while since i read a fantasy book that has no mercy on you. A book that doesn't spare you the gore, the filth and the sadness of the harsh world it depicts. Such books as The lies of Locke Lamora or Prince of thorns and i loved those books. Well, I finally picked up The blade itself and let me tell you, this makes those two look like a children's book. It's Awesome!
This is a Fantasy book but the Fantasy elements i found to be quite light. I mean, they are there and they take an important part in the story but it's nothing over the top and they are almost never at the center of things, instead they become more of a seasoning adding extra flavor to this crazy meal.
The main course here is the characters. They are all unique, carefully crafted and over encumbered with baggage and flaws which makes them more palpable and interesting. None of them is fully evil or good.
There are many characters but the main ones are Logen 9 fingers (an infamous barbarian warrior missing his middle finger), Sand Dan Glokta (a cripple torturer who used to be the hero of the nation), Jezal dan Luthar (a narcissistic young nobleman training for a fencing tournament) and 
Ferro Maljinn (a ruthless young woman hungry for revenge). 
You might think something about them when you first meet them but your opinion of them will probably change many times, as they go through a lot.
Even Though this book is not as ruthless as say something like game of thrones in which characters die every two sentences, here the pain inflicted upon you takes different forms like a character you like going through something horrible or doing something horrible himself. Gory depictions of wounds and vivid descriptions of filth are frequent and they help create a very dark mood for the whole story. 
I'm not getting into the story itself but i'm just gonna say that i thoroughly enjoyed it. Even when nothing happens there will be an interesting interaction between characters or a witty humorous remark that will put a smile in your face. 
I can easily recommend it to any fans of the genre.
reviews.Emperor of Thorns:
To be honest i found that i didn't quiet enjoy this last book the same as i did the previous ones in the trilogy. That is not to say that this book isn't good or it doesn't provide a fitting ending for the story(which it is and it does), but it felt a little bit less focused and. at times a little boring. 
The journey through the book felt overly long, almost like he was providing filler content till what was obvilusly a well planned ending.
And i musy say... Mark always gets me with this twists. i'm usually pretty gopd at guessing twists before they come but these were really unexpected yet they make sense. 
The ending of the book is what saves it in my opinion. It is just pretty fucking good :)
Makes it worth going through most of the parts i didn't quiet enjoy.
reviews.Dark Matter:
First off, i wanna say that if you are new to the genre of sci-fi and have never seen themes like alternate dimensions and such, you might actually like this book. It's not badly written (or narrated if you are listening to the audiobook) and the pacing is pretty engaging at times. However, if you are like me and have seen topics like the ones explored in this book before, then there is absolutely nothing original about it. 
Everything presented here has been done before and in a better way. I won't name the exact events because of spoilers but i'll just say that if you've seen the 90's show Sliders or Stargate, Fringe, Orphan black, the movie Into the spiderverse or a ton of different Marvel or DC comics... then you have most likely seen everything this book has to offer before and will probably not get much enjoyment out of it.
There are one or two reveals that i guess are supposed to be twists but they are just so obvious that they left me wondering whether a bigger twist was ahead (there wasn't).    
To top it off the ending was (in my opinion), both predictable and boring. 
There is absolutely nothing wrong in taking themes and ideas from other pieces of art and making your own thing out of them, as long as you are bringing along something different into the mix that turns it into something new. Sadly, i don't see that here.
reviews.Red Sister:
I loved this book! 
It's been a while since i read Mark Lawrence's previous trilogy (The Red Queen's War) and boy it's good to be back. He's an outstanding author and his books get better and better with each entry.
As in all his previous works, the setting here is dark and harsh. A cold world (Literally and Metaphorically). 
Without going too much into spoiler territory, this is the coming of age story of a traumatized girl who is taken out of jail and adopted by the church of the Ancestor where she is to be trained as a nun. However, nuns in the church of the ancestor are not like the nuns in our world. Instead, they are either Warriors, Witches or even Assassins with great powers.
The World building in this book is great. Unlike many fantasy books i've read lately which bombard you with info dumps, here the exposition is subtle and intriguing. The story encourages you to ask yourself questions about the world of the book and you get your answers little by little as the story progresses. You learn about the ancestor's religion and you keep wondering whether it is real or just make belief and this keeps getting used as a means of further developing the characters. Do they believe or not? are they pretending? What does it say about them? I really liked that.
If Mark Lawrence wants you to know about a people that hasn't appeared in the story yet he might bring up a character who is one of them and use them to introduce this people to you. Same goes for the politics of the world. He explains the empire's structure or the church's structure and hierarchy mostly through the characters. This makes the story way more interesting.   
The timeline also goes back and forth taking interesting turns between memories relived or told by the main character always adding pieces to the puzzle. 
In short, This is a dark and awesome tale with a very interesting setting,  great action scenes and very memorable characters.
reviews.Storm Front:
Have you ever asked yourself what would happen if you blended Buffy the vampire slayer with Angel and Supernatural with a pinch of Scooby Doo? No? Really? Well me neither but the result is an exquisite smoothie that left me hungry for more. Lucky me cause there are like a gazillion entries on this series. 
Is it kitschy? Yup
is it the most incredible thing i have ever read? Nope
Is it fun though? Hell yeah!
You could argue that everything's been done before but there is an originality to cleverly mixing and retelling old stories and i think that is what takes place here. Also if you are going to redo something that's been done before, i believe you have to at least do it perfectly and Jim Butcher might have done just that.
Harry Dresden is 40% constantine, 30% Angel, 10% Van Helsing, 20% Normal Dude. And it is the last part that resonated with me the most actually. I mean yes, he is a wizard and yes, he is charming and witty but he ultimately he is a normal dude with emotions. At times he gets embarrassed and at times he gets scared shitless (many times actually). The fact that he many times overcomes his emotions and the fact that many times he doesn't are to me the most appealing part of his character. It makes him more relatable. 
The story itself is quite simple but it cleverly introduces you to the world of Harry Dresden and the colorful characters that are a part of it. There is a murder mystery and in order to solve it Harry uses different means of magic and contacts different beings and people that pull you into the world he lives in and show you what kind of a man Harry Dresden is.
In conclusion... If you liked any of the references i mentioned above (minus the drama) or are just into a very fun urban fantasy tale i highly recommend this book to you.
On to the next one!
P.S: I heard the audiobook version and it is read by James Marsters who played Spike on Buffy. He did a wonderful job!
reviews.The Path of Daggers:
It's so hard for me to give this book such a low rating because this series has become really dear to me but if i'm completely honest with myself i did not enjoy much of this entry. 
The way i see it, in every story there is this event or mood pattern that tends to appear. Things start dull and normal, there's a complication followed by epic change, things become awesome and then... there's a reality check. a downfall of sorts that makes it seem that nothing is going well. Hopefully that phase is followed by an event that miraculously renews hope and an epic and glorious comeback.
When i think about the phase this book represents for the Wheel of time as a series i think about the downfall and i really hope this phase doesn't prolong itself for too long.
It's a real bummer to be honest, cause up until now every single book had ended with a blast leaving me excited for things to come. This one however, left me feeling anxious for things to be resolved already. 
Without getting too much into detail some of the things i found daunting in this book include: Rand's new and increased hubris, his treatment of the Ashaman, the amount of unresolved mysteries introduced, Perrin's idiotic protectiveness over the Aes Sadai slaves, Cadsuane (i hate her with a passion) and pretty much every female characters interaction with men (although this isn't particular to this book but to the series in general).
I really hope the next book kicks things up a notch. I don't mind it remaining in  the downfall phase but please have it end with an epic resolution like the rest of the books.
reviews.Last Argument of Kings:
Holly shit! What an ending to this awesome trilogy. 
The previous books were rather slow paced and took their time to unwrap the story but this time around it's like Joe Abercrombie said "No time to waste!" and started a crazy sprint to reach the finishing line. And i say it in a good way. I mean, there was absolutely nothing wrong with the previous pace but this time around things go bananas. All out war in all fronts, Magic takes a bigger role, characters take crazy turns and that ending... just wow.
I'm not going to spoil things for you but let's just say that the ending fits magically with the story's personality. It leaves you open mouthed, turning the page to realize there are no more pages left.
reviews.The Well of Ascension:
Man it is hard for me to rate this book so low. Even the three stars i gave it feel a bit much.
Sure there is an awesome Magic system and sure there is some pretty cool world building but i have so many issues with the overall plot of this book that not even the epic sanderson ending could change the sower taste this book left in my mouth.
I'm going to assume that whoever is reading this has already read the previous book so spoiler ahead for said book's ending.
The Lord ruler is dead by the hands of the revolution, the Ska have now taken over luthadel, Ellend is king and the noblemen were left in the government in powerful positions. 
Now... I have trouble believing that a people that's been oppressed for hundreds or maybe thousands of years by a Nazi like empire simply assumes that they will continue to be ruled by the remnants of said empire. I could maybe believe the fact that Ellend is king, if only because he had progressive ideas and the support of the survivor's gang but the other noblemen were terrible and gave no reason to anyone to believe they would change their beliefs (not that it would matter). I find it  ridiculous that any of this would happen or that the people (fueled by the recent uprising) wouldn't revolt again in order to have their own representatives as the sole members of the government. 
Imagine if holocaust survivors were to agree to have the Nazi generals responsible for all what's been done to them, in the government. 
What i think would make much more sense would be something similar to what happened during the french revolution; most noblemen were executed or forced to flee. 
This simple fact ruined so much of the book for me. It made everything so much harder to believe. 
Later on Ellend proves to be a pacifist all the way through. He shows no interest in trying any ploys or assassinations on his enemies and completely makes everything worse for luthadel over and over. I can believe all that but as a reader it becomes quiet annoying after a while. I mean i get it, he doesn't want to be anything that slightly resembles the Lord ruler or the noblemen but he ends up being stupid and not at all a genius as the book seems to suggest. 
spoilers ahead for this book.
After he spends most of the book being a pussy he goes on to out of nowhere stab his friend who is now a psycho. By the way he does that after beating 2 trained soldiers even though he himself is nowhere near as skilled as they should be. So he stabs his friend, threatens him and then leaves. and the soldiers just look at him and do nothing. really? not only that but on the way out of the camp he starts a fight with a giant angry blue creature and wins (did i mention he is not a skilled fighter). And he feels absolutely no guilt over killing the creature. 
vin is another story. I felt that the previous book had a little bit too much soap opera in it with Shan Elariel being Ellend's ex, the rich guy falls in love with the poor girl concept and the story that Marsh had a thing for kalsier's wife, so i was hoping that this book would avoid these silly tropes. However... it seems that Vin has kind of a thing for ellend's secret brother. Really? 
I don't know. There's plenty in this book that i don't like to be honest and in fact by the end i felt that the story hadn't advanced much. It's Sanderson so obviously there's kind of a big twist in the end but i honestly don't think it does much to redeem the rest of the book. not much really happens. I have already started reading the next and i hope it changes my opinion of the series but so far i'm sad to say this series feels quiet overrated.
reviews.King of Thorns:
At first i was a little disappointed with the direction this book was taking. i really liked the fact that the previous book had a no bullshit kind of approach, sparing as the unimportant details and events that too many fantasy writers are eager to tell. However, i felt that it took a long time to ignite and i didn't understand at the time why were these little side quests told to us. 

That being said, during the second half of the book i realized i was dead wrong. Everything has meaning and importance and it builds up background for some really cool twists by the end. I usually guess twists before hand but man i wasn't expecting these at all. The ending is one of my favorites in a long time. so Badass :)

Also i really love some of the concepts touched by this book. For example the main antagonist of the book is basically the man Jorg wishes he'd become but knows will never be. The jealosy and egoism that drive him to hate him are beautifuly built and very understandable.

The post apocalyptic theme revealed in the previous book is further developed here as well and it is so cool. It gives much more depth and mistery to rhe setting.

In short, This book is awesome. very unique in it's perspective. Maybe better than the last one. stay strong during some parts that seem unimportant and be ready for some awesome ending. 
Can't wait to read the next!
reviews.Old Man's War:
It is not often that i stumble upon a book that manages to make me feel like i am the main character. To feel the experiences described by the book's narrator as if they were actually happening to me. Well in this amazing story, masterfully told from a first person point of view i strongly felt like the character in question. 
The story is gripping, fast paced and although it revolves around a heavily sci fi world, it feels somewhat plausible. 
The hero and the rest of the characters that are presented to the reader during the course of the story are believable and interesting. One could easily imagine real people acting like them if they were put in the same situations.
The book also brings along some pretty unique ideas, especially philosophical ones. I more than once found myself wondering about the ethical implications of things. 
In short, i loved this book. It reminded me of Ender's game but with old people.
reviews.Holy Sister:
I've realized after reading a ton of fantasy books that THIS is the way i like it. I might enjoy colorful stories with tons of creatures, races, gods, factions and many overlapping complicated magic systems but in the end what REALLY does it for me is the subtler kind of fantasy. Stories that are not over eager to throw a gargantuan compendium of world building at you, but instead hold secrets from you, tickling that sense of wonder that is probably the main reason most of us avid readers turn to fantasy in the first place. Secrets that make you ask questions constantly and maybe you don't even get all the answers by the end of the road but that only makes you want to come back to the same world so that maybe, you get to reveal more secrets.
That is basically how i feel about Book of the Ancestor. I want to know everything about Abeth, the missing and the four tribes. Even if the story sort of comes to a conclusion, there is a lot more to the story than that. I love that!
Holy sister is exactly what you'd expect it to be after the previous two books. All of the things that were awesome are either still awesome or are elevated to new levels of cool. Character development is key here and it is quite impressive how much the characters grow in this story. The novices grow in a very believable way (especially Nona) and by the end of the book she might even surprise you. 
It is really cool how we are used to protagonists being the most badass in a story and here, although Nona is amazing, she is outshined by Zole.  
Furthermore, i think that this story is filled with such interesting characters that i can easily imagine any one of them as the protagonist of their own stories. 
Think about it. Imagine a story from the perspective of yisht, or kettle, or clera (while she was away), or Zole, or regol (After Holy Sister). I would be totally up for a book of short stories like that! 
Anyways, i really enjoyed the conclusion to this awesome journey and i am stoked to delve deeper into Abeth (i hear the next trilogy is on the same world. SCORE!).
P.S: That Scene with sister Pan... Holly #^&#!
reviews.Circe:
I really don’t get why people like this. 

Retellings of famous stories are in my opinion like a classic culinary dish, meaning that you cook it either exactly like the original (if something ain’t broke don’t fix it style) or you change/add something to elevate the original dish in some way. Anything in between makes me cringe quite a bit because it’s pretentious to begin with to take someone else’s work and make it your own story. You have to honor the original to make it acceptable and this book did nothing of the sort.

Instead of creating her own world with her own characters and magic systems the author took an existing world in the form of greek mythology and didn’t add anything mildly new or interesting to it.

However, the story would have been good if it had had a clear objective in mind. In this story circe is just going through her days and random things happen to her here and there. That’s it. That’s the book. Have fun…
She’s not trying to achieve anything or overcome anything more than a couple hundred year complicated childhood. 

Why do people like this again?
reviews.Warbreaker:
This book is awesome! 
I always complain about how most authors this days are creatively lazy and rely way too much on ideas previously done by other authors. This is especially felt in the fantasy genre where every story seems to be in the same world with the same magic systems.
That being said, nothing could be further from the truth regarding Brandon Sanderson's works and this book is no exception. 
He managed to create a new world with different cultures, religions, and a very beautiful and unique magic system like no other I've seen before. 
The story basically revolves around two sisters, Vivenna and Ciri, alternating between them, although there are a couple more characters which points of view narrations are followed as well such as Vasher(a rugged and powerful man with a talking sword) and Lightsong(a goofy god). One sister is forced to unexpectedly take the other's place as the godking's betrothed and the other is set to try and help her out. I really don't want to reveal anything more about the story itself because it will mostly ruin your experience.
 There are tons of twists and surprises along the way and given the scale of the story, it is quiet impressive that it manages to reach closure by the end of the book.
Also it is notable that there are some ties to the stormlight archive universe so if you are planning on reading the series, this book would come before words of radiance which is the second.
This has just  become my favorite standalone fantasy novel. :)
reviews.Interview with the Vampire:
I am thankful to Anne rice because she inspired works like Buffy the vampire slayer which i grew up watching but to be completely honest, this book is quite boring. Not much really happens through out the whole book. Things which are pretty simple are described to be really complicated and things which could be described quickly end up being the main theme of entire chapters.
Most characters are unrelatable. The book's "hero" doesn't stop whining and brooding about everyone and everything and almost never does anything out of his own initiative.
By the end of the book there is no sudden epiphany or explanation as to why this whole tale is told in the first place and i was left totally underwhelmed. 
I recognize that maybe during the time in which the book was released this might have appeared to be more original or exciting in concept but as for now, i don't think it holds up. 
Also i was really surprised when i found out that the vampire chronicles series focuses mainly on the vampire Lestat. He is in my opinion such an uninteresting character.
reviews.The Way of Kings:
This is most definitely the best world building i have seen in a story in recent years. The characters are awesome but seriously, the world itself is just really impressive.
From the different cultures of peoples presented through the book to the detailed landscapes, everything is believable and original. 
The story takes place mostly in a region called the shattered plains which is a desert like place filled with huge chasms that are really hard to cross for normal humans. An example of the authors attention to detail is the explanation he gives to the shape of this shattered plains. Every now and then there are humongous storms called High storms which are so destructive that hardly any flora or fauna can survive it on the long term, therefore the only creatures that reside in those lands have big sturdy bodies and usually live in the chasms. I don't want to spoil anything else about this but everything in this book has an explanation and it is believable.
There are 3 main story lines that follow 3 main characters although there are many others which are interesting and important overall. The first is a Military man turned slave called Kaladin. The second is an intelligent woman called shalan who goes to study under a famous scholar. The third is Gavilar, the kings uncle and a renowned warrior. The three plots seem distant at first but slowly start to become entangled. To reveal anything else would be basically a spoiler. The characters are deep and flawed but very lovable and relatable and each evolve in their own unique way through the book. 
The last third of the book is filled with twists and mind blowing revelations so be ready.
Also i feel i must warn any new readers as i didn't know this before hand; This is the first book and to the date of this review there are only 3 books out yet but the author has planned it to be a ten book series.
